pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 9.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: CLASS READER

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.4: Reading 9.4.1 Intensive reading: Class Reader

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 9.4.1 Intensive reading: Class Reader. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: What marks the climax of a story?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain the sequence of events in a text

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. explain the sequence of events in a text
   In simple words: practise until you can explain the sequence of events in a text. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 9.4.1 Intensive reading: Class Reader using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 9.4.1 Intensive reading: Class Reader in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 9.4.1 Intensive reading: Class Reader to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 9.4.1 Intensive reading: Class Reader.
4. Show that you can: explain the sequence of events in a text

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 9.4.1 Intensive reading: Class Reader using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 9.4.1 Intensive reading: Class Reader important for a Grade 7 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read sections of a class reader and explain the sequence of events,
2. Collaboration: It is enhanced as the learner participates actively in dramatising parts of the class reader for conceptualisation.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. explain the sequence of events in a text

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.
